text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak Securities Brokers Association (AOCP) and the Finance Ministry on Wednesday opened the second round of discussions about preparations for a new law on collective investment. The ministry said the new law should show a preference for open-end investment funds.

- Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said some 1,200 companies have so far requested inclusion in the so-called revitalisation programme. The scheme is designed to help troubled firms, both state-run and private, overcome their financial problems, with the state and some commercial banks easing the companies' debt burdens for a certain period.
- But Kozlik said only a limited amount of firms will be included in the revitalisation plsn, mainly companies which are the main employers in their regions.

- Opposition Christain Democratic Movement (KDH) leader Jan Carnogursky has called for parliament to return the mandate to Jozef Gaulieder who was expelled from parliament last December. Carnogursky said such a move would have a strong positive effect on Slovakia's image abroad.

SME - The Slovak Democratic Coalition (SDK), which groups five main opposition parties, is expected in September to sign a treaty with the ethnic Hungarian Colaition on cooperation after the 1998 general elections.

PRAVDA - Slovakia's lawyers at the Hague's International Court in a case against Hungary over the controversial Gabcikovo dam on the River Danube said that they did not expect a ruling that would force Slovakia to destroy the dam and the already operating power plant.

- Slovakia is expected to start demanding fees for using its highways in the year 2001. The fees, planned for 0.80 crowns per kilometre, should total some 135 billion crowns between the years 2001 and 2019.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak Antimonopoly Office said it had imposed fines worth 5.4 million crowns for violation of competetiton rules in the first half of this year.
- Slovakia's imports from Russia now exceed five times its exports.
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - The agricultural trade fair Agrokomplex began on Wednesday in the western Slovak town of Nitra.
- The governemnt is planning to increase the minimum wage to some 3,000 crowns from the beginning of next year.
